desc: Fix odd_part implementation (current version has bugs: should be `x >> (x & -x).bit_length() - 1` or use `x // (x & -x)` to get the odd part)
Verify sample inputs 1, 2, 3 with current solution
Optimize FFT: use real-valued FFT or numpy.fft for speed (pure Python FFT on size ~2^25 will be too slow)
Ensure FFT size is correct and avoids circular convolution (size >= 2*max(A)+1)
Handle integer rounding correctly after inverse FFT (use int(round(x.real)) carefully)
Test edge cases (N=1, all same values, large N)

If time-critical, consider alternative approach: since A_i ≤ 10^7, we can iterate over odd parts separately: for each odd v, count numbers of form v*2^k, then compute contributions using convolution over smaller ranges per v. This avoids large FFT.
Alternative O(N * sqrt(maxA)) approach: iterate over odd v up to maxA, and for each v, do convolution on the array of counts of v*2^k. This reduces FFT size significantly.
